<content>
1: ## Why
2: 
3: The install scripts are the reason a full `chezmoi apply` has been off limits since 2026-10-26: `05-install` would lower the system open-files limit, uninstall undeclared brew packages, compile YouCompleteMe, prompt for GitHub login and reinstall a retired extension, all because a package list changed.
4: Other scripts never re-run when their inputs change, or redo work on every run.
5: Scripts must become safe to run at any time before the supervised apply (audit findings F01, F02, F24 for scripts, F27).
6: 
7: ## What Changes
8: 
9: - **BREAKING (behaviour)**: `run_onchange_before_05-install.sh.tmpl` is split into focused after-scripts, one per manager, each triggered by its own input: brew (Brewfile), mise (`config.toml`), pipx (`packages.json`), krew (`packages.yaml`), vim plugins (`vimrc`).
10: - No script uninstalls anything: `brew file clean` is replaced by a dry-run report of what is undeclared.
11: - The open-files limit comes from data, is written only when the file differs, and is never lowered.
12: - `gh auth login` and the gh-copilot install are dropped; YouCompleteMe is built only on request and only when missing.
13: - The apt prerequisites script is guarded to the Debian family, installs only missing packages, and calls sudo only then; its list moves to `.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`.
14: - Broken trigger lines (`\{\{ ... \}\}`) become real hashes; the bat cache script also hashes its themes.
15: - The VSCodium script skips `.vsix` files whose extension is installed.
16: - Scripts share a small helper (logging, dry-run mode, sudo guard) and contain no user-specific paths.
17: 
18: ## Capabilities
19: 
20: ### New Capabilities
21: 
22: - `install-scripts`: what chezmoi's scripts may do, when they run, and how they are checked.
23: 
24: ### Modified Capabilities
25: 
26: None.
27: 
28: ## Impact
29: 
30: - `.chezmoiscripts/`: one script removed, several added or renamed; every script's content changes, so each runs once on the next apply (designed to be a no-op on a provisioned machine).
31: - `.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`: apt list and limits data.
32: - New `.chezmoitemplates/script-lib.sh`.
33: - Package sets and installed software are unchanged by this change.
34:

(End of file - total 35 lines)

<content>
1: ## Context
2: 
3: Scripts on commit `191ee9e` (paths under `home/` after `adopt-chezmoiroot`), see audit section 2.3:
4: 
5: - `run_onchange_before_00-pre-requesites.sh.tmpl`: not templated, no guard, `sudo apt-get update` and install of 12 packages on every content change.
6: - `run_onchange_before_05-install.sh.tmpl` (linux branch):
7:   - line 5: escaped, inert mise hash;
8:   - lines 11, 15-16: `ulimit -n 20480`, then overwrites `/etc/security/limits.d/ulimit.conf` with 20480/40960 (live: 32768/65536);
9:   - lines 18-28: brew-file variables, `HOMEBREW_BREWFILE` pointing into the source, `Brewfile.backup` spelling differs from the config's `brewfile.backup`;
10:   - lines 30-32: Homebrew plus brew-file through brew-file's installer, then `brew shellenv` from a literal path;
11:   - lines 39-41: Brewfile hash, `brew file install`, `brew file clean -V warning` (uninstalls undeclared packages, untaps, wipes the cache);
12:   - line 49: `rustup default stable`;
13:   - lines 52-68: mise block, commented out;
14:   - lines 70-73: pipx hash and `pipx install-all` from the source path;
15:   - lines 75-79: `vim +PluginInstall +qall` (before Vundle and vimrc exist on a new machine), YouCompleteMe `install.py --all`;
16:   - lines 81-82: `gh auth login` when not logged in, `gh extension install github/gh-copilot`.
17: - `run_onchange_before_10-install-packages.sh.tmpl`: `kubectl krew install` of all 7 plugins (darwin: `brew bundle`).
18: - `run_onchange_before_decrypt-private-key.sh.tmpl`: literal home path; sorts after `10-` today.
19: - `run_onchange_after_20-vscodium-extensions.sh.tmpl`: good list logic; `.vsix` loop at lines 23-26 reinstalls every time.
20: - `run_onchange_after_bat-cache-build.sh.tmpl`: escaped, inert hash at line 5.
21: 
22: chezmoi runs `run_before_` scripts, then updates files and externals, then `run_after_` scripts, each group in name order.
23: `run_onchange_` state is keyed by the rendered content's hash: any edit makes the script run once more; renaming alone does not.
24: 
25: ## Goals / Non-Goals
26: 
27: **Goals:**
28: 
29: - Every script is safe to run at any time: idempotent, non-interactive, no removals, sudo only when a change is needed.
30: - Every script re-runs exactly when its declared input changes.
31: - Scripts can be exercised without side effects (dry-run mode).
32: 
33: **Non-Goals:**
34: 
35: - Changing which packages are declared or which manager owns a tool (change `rationalize-package-ownership`).
36: - Distro and profile data beyond a Debian-family guard (change `fresh-machine-bootstrap`).
37: - macOS branches: kept as they are, untested.
38: 
39: ## Decisions
40: 
41: ### New script set
42: 
43: | Script | Phase | Trigger (hashed input) | Does |
44: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
45: | `run_onchange_before_00-prerequisites.sh.tmpl` | before | `packages.linux.apt` | Debian family only; installs missing apt packages; sudo only if some are missing |
46: | `run_onchange_before_01-decrypt-private-key.sh.tmpl` | before | content | unchanged logic, `$HOME` instead of a literal path |
47: | `run_onchange_before_02-system-limits.sh.tmpl` | before | `system.limits` | writes the limits file only when it differs and never with lower values; sudo only then |
48: | `run_onchange_after_10-brew.sh.tmpl` | after | Brewfile | Homebrew and brew-file if missing; `brew file install` against the deployed `~/.config/brewfile/Brewfile`; prints `brew file clean --dry-run` output as a report; `rustup default stable` only when no default toolchain |
49: | `run_onchange_after_11-mise.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/mise/config.toml` | `mise install --yes` |
50: | `run_onchange_after_12-pipx.sh.tmpl` | after | `packages.json` | installs only venvs missing from `pipx list --short`, through a filtered copy of the spec file |
51: | `run_onchange_after_13-krew.sh.tmpl` | after | `packages.linux.krews` | installs only missing plugins (darwin `brew bundle` part kept in its own darwin branch) |
52: | `run_onchange_after_20-vscodium-extensions.sh.tmpl` | after | extension list | as today; `.vsix` skipped when its `publisher.name` is installed |
53: | `run_onchange_after_30-vim-plugins.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/vim/vimrc` | `vim -Es -u ~/.vimrc +PluginInstall +qall`; YouCompleteMe build only when `vim.ycm_build` is true and the core library is missing |
54: | `run_onchange_after_90-bat-cache.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/bat/config`, `.chezmoiexternals/bat.toml.tmpl` | `bat cache --build` |
55: 
56: Hash lines use `{{ include "<path>" | sha256sum }}` or `{{ .<data> | toJson | sha256sum }}`; nothing escaped.
57: Package managers move to after-scripts so they read deployed files (Brewfile, `packages.json`, `vimrc`) instead of source paths, and so vim plugins install after Vundle (an external) and the vimrc exist.
58: 
59: ### Shared helper
60: 
61: `.chezmoitemplates/script-lib.sh`, included with `{{ template "script-lib.sh" . }}`, provides:
62: 
63: - `log` (prefixed with the script name, to stderr);
64: - `run` (executes, or prints when `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`);
65: - `as_root` (calls sudo through `run`, logs why);
66: - `have` (`command -v` wrapper);
67: - `set -euo pipefail`.
68: 
69: ### No removals
70: 
71: Uninstalling stays a deliberate human action.
72: The brew script prints what `brew file clean` would remove so drift is visible on every run that matters.
73: 
74: ### Data added to `.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`
75: 
76: - `packages.linux.apt`: the 12 packages of the prerequisites script (key `dpkgs` renamed, it is empty and unused).
77: - `system.limits.nofile`: `soft: 32768`, `hard: 65536` (live values on 2026-10-30).
78: - `vim.ycm_build: false`.
79: - `brew.prefix: /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`, the only place the Homebrew prefix is written.
80: 
81: ## Risks / Trade-offs
82: 
83: - [Risk] Every script runs once on the next apply because its content changed. → Each is a no-op on this machine by design; proved with dry-run mode and a sudo stub before the supervised apply.
84: - [Risk] Moving brew, pipx and mise to after-scripts means files that need those tools (templates calling `output "aqua"` and similar) render before the tools exist on a fresh machine. → Unchanged from today for this machine; a fresh machine is handled in `fresh-machine-bootstrap`, which may move only the brew bootstrap back to a before-script.
85: - [Risk] `pipx install-all` on a filtered file loses injected packages or Python pins. → Filter with `jq` on the `venvs` keys only, keeping each venv's full metadata.
86: - [Risk] Dropping `gh auth login` leaves a fresh machine without gh auth. → gh reads the token from the encrypted environment; the brew script logs a warning when `gh auth status` fails.
87: - [Trade-off] The dry-run variable is a local convention, not a chezmoi feature; documented in `AGENTS.md`.
88: 
89: ## Open Questions
90: 
91: - Keep Vundle and the vim plugins at all, now that Neovim is the editor? (Default: keep, without YouCompleteMe.)
92: - Should the brew undeclared-package report also cover mise (`mise prune --dry-run`) and pipx? (Default: brew only here; the rest in `rationalize-package-ownership`.)
93:

<content>
1: ## ADDED Requirements
2: 
3: ### Requirement: Scripts are no-ops on an up-to-date machine
4: 
5: Every chezmoi script SHALL install nothing, write nothing outside `$HOME`, and call no sudo when the machine already matches its inputs.
6: 
7: #### Scenario: Run each script on the provisioned laptop
8: 
9: - **WHEN** each script is rendered with `chezmoi execute-template` and run with a `sudo` stub first on `PATH` that records any call
10: - **THEN** the stub records nothing and the script exits 0
11: 
12: #### Scenario: Second run in a row
13: 
14: - **WHEN** a script that installed something is run again immediately
15: - **THEN** it installs nothing
16: 
17: ### Requirement: Scripts never uninstall
18: 
19: No script SHALL uninstall packages, remove taps, or delete caches; drift is reported instead.
20: 
21: #### Scenario: Undeclared brew package
22: 
23: - **WHEN** a brew package is installed but absent from the Brewfile and the brew script runs
24: - **THEN** the package is still installed afterwards and the script output names it as undeclared
25: 
26: ### Requirement: System files written only when needed and never weakened
27: 
28: A script that manages a file outside `$HOME` SHALL write it only when its content differs from the declared data, and SHALL never lower a limit.
29: 
30: #### Scenario: Limits already match
31: 
32: - **WHEN** `/etc/security/limits.d/ulimit.conf` holds the declared open-files limits and the limits script runs
33: - **THEN** the file is untouched and no sudo call happens
34: 
35: #### Scenario: Declared value lower than the live one
36: 
37: - **WHEN** the declared limit is lower than the value in the file
38: - **THEN** the script logs a warning and leaves the file unchanged
39: 
40: ### Requirement: Non-interactive scripts
41: 
42: Scripts SHALL never prompt, except the identity decryption, which asks for its passphrase only when the identity file is missing.
43: 
44: #### Scenario: No terminal
45: 
46: - **WHEN** a rendered script other than the identity decryption runs with standard input from `/dev/null`
47: - **THEN** it completes without waiting for input
48: 
49: ### Requirement: Triggers follow inputs
50: 
51: Each `run_onchange_` script SHALL embed a hash of every input it acts on, so a change to that input, and only to it, makes the script run again.
52: 
53: #### Scenario: Input change re-renders the script
54: 
55: - **WHEN** a script's declared input file or data changes
56: - **THEN** `chezmoi execute-template` of that script produces different output
57: 
58: #### Scenario: No escaped template actions
59: 
60: - **WHEN** `grep -rn '\\{\\{' .chezmoiscripts/` runs in the source state
61: - **THEN** it prints nothing
62: 
63: ### Requirement: Portable scripts
64: 
65: Scripts SHALL contain no user-specific absolute path and SHALL guard distro-specific commands.
66: 
67: #### Scenario: No literal home or source path
68: 
69: - **WHEN** `rg -n '/home/[a-z]+/|\.local/share/chezmoi' .chezmoiscripts/` runs in the source state
70: - **THEN** it prints nothing (the Homebrew prefix comes from data)
71: 
72: #### Scenario: apt only on the Debian family
73: 
74: - **WHEN** the prerequisites script is rendered on a system whose os-release id and id_like do not include `debian`
75: - **THEN** the rendered script is empty
76: 
77: ### Requirement: Dry-run mode
78: 
79: Scripts SHALL honour `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1` by printing each action instead of performing it.
80: 
81: #### Scenario: Dry run of the brew script
82: 
83: - **WHEN** the rendered brew script runs with `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`
84: - **THEN** it prints the commands it would run and changes nothing
85: 
86: ### Requirement: Shell quality
87: 
88: Rendered scripts SHALL pass shellcheck.
89: 
90: #### Scenario: shellcheck on rendered scripts
91: 
92: - **WHEN** each script is rendered and passed to `shellcheck -s bash`
93: - **THEN** it reports no error
94:

16:   if grep -qxF "${ext,,}" <<<"${installed}"; then
17:     continue
18:   fi
19:   codium --install-extension "${ext}" || echo "vscodium-extensions: failed: ${ext}" >&2
20: done
21: 
22: # Extensions that are not on Open VSX: .vsix files kept outside this repository.
23: for vsix in "${HOME}"/.local/share/vsix/*.vsix; do
24:   [ -e "${vsix}" ] || continue
25:   codium --install-extension "${vsix}" || echo "vscodium-extensions: failed: ${vsix}" >&2
26: done
27: {{- end }}

{{- $is_codespaces:= env "CODESPACES" | not | not }}

[data.github]
  is_codespaces = {{ $is_codespaces }}
== home/.chezmoitemplates/machine-type.toml.tmpl
{{- $machineType := "desktop" }}
{{- $is_codespaces:= env "CODESPACES" | not | not -}}
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }}
{{-   if contains "MacBook" (output "/usr/sbin/system_profiler" "SPHardwareDataType") }}
{{-     $machineType = "laptop" }}
{{-   else }}
{{-     $machineType = "desktop" }}
{{-   end }}
{{- else if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" }}
{{-   if $is_codespaces }}
{{-     $machineType = "virtual" }}
{{-   else }}
{{-     $machineType = (output "hostnamectl" "--json=short" | mustFromJson).Chassis }}
{{-   end }}
{{- else if eq .chezmoi.os "windows" }}
{{-   $machineType = (output "powershell.exe" "-NoProfile" "-NonInteractive" "-Command" "if ((Get-CimInstance -Class Win32_Battery | Measure-Object).Count -gt 0) { Write-Output 'laptop' } else { Write-Output 'desktop' }") | trim }}
{{- end }}

[data.machine]
  type = {{ $machineType | quote }}

{{/* detect OS */}}
{{- $osid := .chezmoi.os -}}

{{- end -}}
{{- $wsl2 := and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") ( .chezmoi.kernel.osrelease | lower | contains "microsoft" ) -}}
{{- $windows_sandbox := and (eq .chezmoi.os "windows") ( .chezmoi.username | contains "WDAGUtilityAccount" ) -}}

{{/* detect macOS version */}}
{{- $macos_version := "" -}}
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}

{{- $hostName := .chezmoi.hostname -}}

{{/*- $hostExternals := or (get $hostConfig "externals") list -*/}}

117: ## 3. Status on 2026-10-30
118: 
119: ```text
120:  R .chezmoiscripts/05-install.sh            Brewfile and packages.json changed since its last run (2025-12-01)
121:  R .chezmoiscripts/20-vscodium-extensions.sh new, never run
122: MM .config/lazygit/config.yml

124:  M .config/brewfile/Brewfile                 mode 0644 -> 0664
125: MM .config, .local/share/fonts, .local/share/icons, three LXQt theme dirs (modes)
126: ```
127: 
128: - A full `chezmoi apply` has been avoided on purpose since 2026-10-26 because of `F01`.
129: - Shell startup measured with `zsh -i -c exit`: 2.5 s (2.5 to 3.6 s over runs); `zsh -l -i -c exit`: 7.0 s.
130: - `chezmoi doctor`: newer version available, suspicious entry `dot_config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml.tmpl`.
131: 
132: ## 4. Findings
133: 
134: ### High
135: 
136: - **F01**: re-running `05-install` is unsafe.
137:   - Lines 15-16 overwrite `/etc/security/limits.d/ulimit.conf` with 20480/40960, lower than the live 32768/65536.
138:   - Line 41 runs `brew file clean`, which is not a dry run: it uninstalls undeclared packages (today the `whosthere` cask), untaps, and empties the brew cache.
139:   - Lines 75-79 run `vim +PluginInstall` before Vundle and the vimrc are deployed (before script), then a full YouCompleteMe build.
140:   - Line 81 may start an interactive `gh auth login`; line 82 reinstalls the deprecated gh-copilot extension under `set -e`.
141:   - Lines 18 and 73 hard-code the source directory path.
142: - **F02**: trigger lines that never trigger.
143:   `05-install.sh.tmpl:5` (mise config) and `bat-cache-build.sh.tmpl:5` (bat config) escape the braces (`\{\{ ... \}\}`), so they are comments and edits never re-run the scripts.
144:   The mise block of `05-install` (lines 52-68) is commented out, so nothing runs `mise install`.
145: - **F03**: `dot_config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml.tmpl` is a frozen rendered config applied over the generated one.
146:   It carries stale data (4 cores, 8 threads, `desktop`, where a fresh render gives 6, 12 and `laptop`) and is the only place encryption is configured.
147: - **F04**: a fresh `chezmoi init --apply` cannot decrypt.
148:   `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` has no `encryption` or `[age]` section, so encrypted targets fail until the snapshot of `F03` is deployed.
149: - **F05**: `~/.config/nvim` had a single copy (no remote, uncommitted work).
150:   A private remote is being created on 2026-10-30; the repository should then come in as a chezmoi external.
151: - **F06**: zsh login shells run `rc.d` twice (2.6 diagram), 7.0 s instead of 2.5 s, with duplicate side effects (banners, completions, `PATH` work).
152:   tmux starts login shells, so every new pane pays it.
153: 
154: ### Medium
155: 
156: - **F07**: `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:51` writes `diff.exclude` inside `[diff]`, giving the key `diff.diff.exclude`; `chezmoi dump-config` shows `diff.exclude: []`.
157: - **F08**: `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:16-18` (`pager`, `color`) come after the tables emitted by the included templates, so they land in `[data.github]`; the effective pager is `less`.
158: - **F09**: `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:30` uses `promptString` (asks on every init) without `quote` for a commit message template that is unused (`autoCommit = false`).
159: - **F10**: at least one encrypted target is deployed group-readable because its source name lacks `private_`.
160:   Lookup: `chezmoi managed --include=encrypted --path-style=absolute | xargs stat -c '%a %n'`.
161: - **F11**: two chezmoi binaries; the older one (`~/.local/bin`, 2.62.2) wins on `PATH`.
162: - **F12**: this public repository has no secret scanning, neither in history nor at commit time.
163: - **F13**: with umask 002, chezmoi would make managed directories and files group-writable (`~/.config`, `~/.local/share/fonts`, `icons`, LXQt theme dirs) and open `~/.config/VSCodium` from 0700 to 0775; the Brewfile shows a mode-only diff after each brew change (brew-file writes 0644).

198: 
199: - Work is planned and tracked with OpenSpec only (same workflow and `/opsx-*` commands as the Neovim repository).
200: - The source state moves into `home/` (`.chezmoiroot`) early, so repository files (`openspec/`, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, tooling) sit outside chezmoi's scope.

# chezmoi-config Specification

## Purpose

How chezmoi's own configuration is produced and what it must contain: generated by `chezmoi init` from the template, with encryption, restrictive modes, working keys, the Incus flag and a Brewfile that stays in sync.

## Requirements
### Requirement: Config generated from the template only

chezmoi's configuration SHALL be produced by `chezmoi init` from `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, and no managed target SHALL overwrite it.

#### Scenario: Config file is not managed

- **WHEN** `chezmoi managed | grep -c '^\.config/chezmoi/chezmoi\.toml$'` runs
- **THEN** it prints 0

#### Scenario: Doctor has no suspicious entry

- **WHEN** `chezmoi doctor` runs
- **THEN** no `suspicious-entries` warning is reported

#### Scenario: Data matches the machine

- **WHEN** `chezmoi data --format=json | jq -c '{c: .cpu, m: .machine}'` runs on a laptop
- **THEN** the machine type is `laptop` and the cpu counts equal `lscpu`'s cores and threads

### Requirement: Encryption configured by the template

The template SHALL set `encryption = "age"` and the `[age]` identity and recipient, so a freshly initialized machine can decrypt once the identity exists.

#### Scenario: Render without a stored config

- **WHEN** `chezmoi --override-data '{"email":"x","gitemail":"x","firstname":"x","name":"x"}' execute-template --init < home/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` output is parsed as TOML
- **THEN** it has `encryption = "age"`, an `age.identity` and an `age.recipient`

#### Scenario: Encrypted targets still decrypt

- **WHEN** `chezmoi cat` runs on any encrypted target after `chezmoi init`
- **THEN** it exits 0

### Requirement: Every key takes effect

Top-level keys SHALL precede all tables and included templates, and each table key SHALL use chezmoi's documented name.

#### Scenario: Effective settings

- **WHEN** `chezmoi dump-config --format=json | jq -c '{u: .umask, p: .pager, c: .color, d: .diff.exclude}'` runs
- **THEN** umask is 23 (octal 027), pager is `bat`, color is `"auto"`, and diff exclude is `["externals"]`

#### Scenario: No data pollution

- **WHEN** `chezmoi data --format=json | jq '.github | keys'` runs
- **THEN** it lists only `is_codespaces`

#### Scenario: Init does not prompt when data exists

- **WHEN** `chezmoi init` runs on a machine whose config already holds every value the template prompts for (identity, Neovim location, Incus flag)
- **THEN** it asks no question

### Requirement: The config records whether Incus is wanted

The template SHALL ask once whether Incus is wanted on the machine, with default no, and SHALL emit the answer as `features.incus` in a `[data.features]` table, so that it survives `chezmoi init`.

#### Scenario: Answer is recorded

- **WHEN** `chezmoi --override-data '{"email":"x","gitemail":"x","firstname":"x","name":"x","features":{"incus":true}}' execute-template --init < home/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl | python3 -c 'import sys,tomllib; print(tomllib.loads(sys.stdin.read())["data"]["features"]["incus"])'` runs
- **THEN** it prints `True`

#### Scenario: Default is no

- **WHEN** the same command runs without the `features` key in the override data and with standard input not attached to a terminal
- **THEN** it prints `False`

#### Scenario: Table does not pollute another one

- **WHEN** `chezmoi data --format=json | jq -c '.github | keys'` runs after `chezmoi init`
- **THEN** it lists only `is_codespaces`

### Requirement: Restrictive deployment modes

chezmoi SHALL deploy with umask 027: files 0640, executables and directories 0750, private entries 0600 or 0700.

#### Scenario: Expected mode of a plain file

- **WHEN** a plain managed file is applied alone with `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <target>`
- **THEN** `stat -c '%a' <target>` prints 640

### Requirement: Brewfile stays in sync after brew changes

After brew changes the Brewfile, the brew hook SHALL leave both the source and the target in sync, mode included.

#### Scenario: No mode-only drift

- **WHEN** a brew install or uninstall through brew-wrap finishes and the hook has run
- **THEN** `chezmoi status ~/.config/brewfile/Brewfile` prints nothing

# neovim-config Specification

## Purpose

Where the Neovim configuration comes from and how it is kept safe from the external: the location is local chezmoi data, the clone is a `git-repo` external that never overwrites local work.

## Requirements
### Requirement: Neovim location is configuration

The host, owner and repository of the Neovim configuration SHALL come from chezmoi data kept in the local config, never from a tracked file.

#### Scenario: Data keys

- **WHEN** `chezmoi data --format=json | jq -c '.nvim | keys'` runs after `chezmoi init`
- **THEN** it prints `["host","owner","repo"]`

### Requirement: Neovim configuration from its own repository

The Neovim configuration SHALL be cloned from its repository by a chezmoi external that never overwrites local work.

#### Scenario: Missing directory is cloned

- **WHEN** `~/.config/nvim` does not exist, the data is set, a GitHub CLI login file exists, and `chezmoi apply --include=externals --exclude=scripts ~/.config/nvim` runs
- **THEN** the repository is cloned there and the URL of its `origin` remote equals the one built from the configured host, owner and repository

#### Scenario: Existing clone keeps its work

- **WHEN** `~/.config/nvim` exists with local commits or uncommitted changes and `chezmoi apply --include=externals --exclude=scripts -R --force ~/.config/nvim` runs
- **THEN** `git -C ~/.config/nvim status -sb` lists the same changes, and `HEAD` is unchanged or advanced only by a fast-forward

#### Scenario: No data, no external

- **WHEN** `nvim.owner` or `nvim.repo` is empty and `chezmoi managed | grep -c '^\.config/nvim$'` runs
- **THEN** it prints 0

#### Scenario: No clone and no GitHub login

# source-layout Specification

## Purpose

Where the chezmoi source state lives inside the repository and what stays outside it, so that no repository file can become a target by accident.

## Requirements
### Requirement: Source state under home/

The chezmoi source state SHALL live in the `home/` directory of the repository, selected by a `.chezmoiroot` file at the repository root.

#### Scenario: Source directory

- **WHEN** `chezmoi source-path` runs
- **THEN** it prints the repository path followed by `/home`

#### Scenario: No source entries at the root

- **WHEN** `git ls-files | grep -vx '.chezmoiroot' | grep -E '^(dot_|symlink_|empty_|private_|executable_|\.chezmoi[a-z]+)'` runs at the repository root
- **THEN** it prints nothing (`.chezmoiroot` itself is the one special file that stays at the root)

### Requirement: Repository files stay outside the source state

Files that run the repository (agent guide, docs, specs, tool pins, hooks, bootstrap script, README) SHALL live outside `home/` and SHALL need no `.chezmoiignore` entry.

#### Scenario: No repository entries in the ignore file

- **WHEN** `grep -nE '^(AGENTS\.md|README\.md|TODO\.md|docs|openspec|scripts|mise\.toml|hk\.pkl)$' home/.chezmoiignore` runs
- **THEN** it prints nothing

#### Scenario: Repository files are not targets

- **WHEN** `chezmoi managed | grep -E '^(AGENTS\.md|README\.md|docs|openspec|scripts|mise\.toml|hk\.pkl)'` runs
- **THEN** it prints nothing

### Requirement: The layout move changes no target

Moving the source state SHALL leave the managed target list, the target state and the pending scripts unchanged.

#### Scenario: Before and after snapshots match

- **WHEN** `chezmoi managed`, `chezmoi status` and `chezmoi diff --exclude=externals` are captured before and after the move
- **THEN** each pair is identical, except script entries whose content changed only by a source path fix

### Requirement: No hard-coded source path

Templates and scripts SHALL reach source files through `.chezmoi.sourceDir` or relative `include` calls, never through a literal path.

#### Scenario: No literal source path

- **WHEN** `rg -n '\.local/share/chezmoi' home/` runs
- **THEN** it prints nothing

<!-- vim: set ts=2 sts=2 sw=2 et endofline fixendofline spell spl=en : -->

{{- /*
  Neovim configuration, cloned from its own repository.
  The location (host, owner, repository) is local data (chezmoi init), never written here.
  No data, or neither a clone nor a GitHub CLI login file: no external.
  refreshPeriod 0 and a fast-forward-only pull: local work is never merged over, rebased or discarded.
*/ -}}
{{- $nvim := or (get . "nvim") dict -}}
{{- $owner := get $nvim "owner" -}}
{{- $repo := get $nvim "repo" -}}
{{- $host := or (get $nvim "host") "github.com" -}}
{{- $hasClone := stat (joinPath .chezmoi.destDir ".config" "nvim" ".git") -}}
{{- $hasLogin := stat (joinPath .chezmoi.destDir ".config" "gh" "hosts.yml") -}}
{{- if and $owner $repo (or $hasClone $hasLogin) }}
[".config/nvim"]
  type = "git-repo"
  url = {{ printf "https://%s/%s/%s.git" $host $owner $repo | quote }}
  refreshPeriod = "0"
  pull.args = ["--ff-only"]
{{- else if and $owner $repo }}
{{ warnf "nvim: no clone and no GitHub CLI login, skipping the Neovim external" }}
{{- end }}

        # Update
        if self.opt['command'] == 'update':
            with self.DryrunBanner(self):
                if not self.opt['noupgradeatupdate']:
                    _ = self.helper.proc(
                        'brew update',
                        dryrun=self.opt['dryrun'],
                    )
                    fetch_head = (
                        '--fetch-HEAD' if self.opt['fetch_head'] else ''
                    )
                    _ = self.helper.proc(
                        f'brew upgrade --formula {fetch_head}',
                        dryrun=self.opt['dryrun'],
                    )
                    if is_mac():
                        _ = self.helper.proc(
                            'brew upgrade --cask',
                            dryrun=self.opt['dryrun'],
                        )
                if self.opt['repo'] != '':
                    self.repomgr('pull')
                self.install()
                self.cleanup(delete_cache=False)
                if not self.opt['dryrun']:
                    _ = self.initialize(check=False, debug_out=True)
                if self.opt['repo'] != '':
                    self.repomgr('push')
            return

        # No command found
        msg = (
            f'Wrong command: {self.opt["command"]}\n'
            f'Execute `{__prog__} help` for more information.'
        )

```

### Facts checked read-only that change the design

1. **Renaming a `run_onchange_` script makes it run again.**
   chezmoi keeps their state in `entryState`, keyed by target path (`~/.chezmoiscripts/05-install.sh`, and so on), not by content hash.
   The design's claim at line 23 is wrong.
   The outcome is the same here, because every script's content changes anyway.
   Keys for removed scripts stay in the state database: I'll record them for `reconcile-drift-and-supervised-apply` and won't delete them.
2. **brew-file 10.2.2 ignores casks on Linux.**
   Installs, cleanup and Brewfile writes all go through `is_mac()`.
   `whosthere` is a cask, so `brew file clean` never removes it and its dry run never names it, which makes the example in F01 and task 4.1 wrong.
   The real risk is still there: undeclared formulae are uninstalled, taps are removed, `brew cleanup` runs and the brew cache is deleted.
   In brew-file's code, every one of those actions respects `--dry-run`.
3. **Live state:**
   - limits are 32768/65536, matching the planned data;
   - krew 7 of 7;
   - pipx: 23 declared, 28 installed, 0 missing, 5 undeclared;
   - `rustup default` is set and `gh auth status` succeeds;
   - YouCompleteMe's core library is built (`ycm_core*.so`, py313 and py314) and 52 Vundle plugins are present;
   - there is one `.vsix` (`sitoi.ai-commit`), already installed. Its ID can be read with `unzip -p … extension/package.json | jq`.
4. **The Debian guard can be tested.** `--override-data '{"chezmoi":{"osRelease":{"id":"fedora","idLike":"rhel"}}}'` does override `.chezmoi.osRelease`.
5. **Proof tools exist.** mise 2026.9.5 has `install --dry-run-code`, and pipx 1.17.2 `install-all` accepts a spec file.
6. **The design's line numbers for `05-install` are still correct.** Only the two layout commits have touched the scripts since `191ee9e`.

### How each task is proved without touching the machine

Harness in `/tmp/opencode/scripts-test/` (mode 0700): it renders every script with `chezmoi -S <wt> execute-template`, then runs it with stdin from `/dev/null`. It has two modes:
- **Isolated:**
  - stubs come first on `PATH` (`sudo`, `apt-get`, `dpkg-query`, `brew`, `pipx`, `mise`, `kubectl`, `codium`, `vim`, `gh`, `rustup`, `bat`, `chezmoi`, `unzip`);
  - each stub logs its arguments and returns canned output from fixtures;
  - `HOME` is a scratch directory.
  This proves the logic both ways: install when something is missing, no call when up to date, never uninstall, dry-run printing.
- **Live read-only:**
  - real `HOME`, with `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`;
  - the stubs forward an allow-list of read-only calls to the real tools (`dpkg-query -W`, `brew list`, `brew file clean|install --dry-run`, `pipx list`, `kubectl krew list`, `codium --list-extensions`, `rustup default` with no argument, `gh auth status`, `mise install --dry-run-code`);
  - every other call is refused and logged.
  The script passes on this laptop when it exits 0 and both the refused log and the sudo log are empty.

### Open-files limit (`before_05`)

- The script's own `ulimit -n 20480` goes away. It only changed the script's own process anyway.
- If the data key is missing, the script renders empty and the current file stays as it is.
- Something I found while checking: the 32768 soft limit never reaches your KDE session.
  `plasmashell` and your zsh processes see 1024 soft and 65536 hard, because the systemd user manager applies `DefaultLimitNOFILESoft=1024`.
  The file only affects PAM login sessions (TTY, ssh).
  Raising the soft limit in the desktop session would need a systemd `user.conf` drop-in. That would be a separate follow-up, not part of this change.

### pipx: make the declared list match what is installed

- I'd regenerate `home/dot_config/pipx/packages.json` from `pipx list --json`. That gives 28 venvs: the 23 already declared plus calcure, euporie, hike, ipython and pynvim.

### D6: krew on other systems

      Run oneliner script:

  caveats: |

YouCompleteMe is built only on request and only when missing.\n- The apt prerequisites script is guarded to the Debian family, installs only missing packages, and calls sudo only then; its list moves to `home/.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`.\n- The krew script has one branch per operating system (Linux and macOS): the plugin list is a shared list `packages.common.krews` plus a list per system; the darwin `brew bundle` call moves to the darwin branch of the brew script.\n- `home/dot_config/pipx/packages.json` is synchronized with the 28 venvs installed on this machine, so that the undeclared report starts empty.\n- Broken trigger lines (`\\{\\{ ... \\}\\}`) become real hashes; **Output:**
```
# Use scripts to perform actions

## Understand how scripts work

chezmoi supports scripts that are executed when you run [`chezmoi
apply`][apply-command]. These scripts can be configured to run every time, only
when their contents have changed, or only if they haven't been run before.

Scripts are any file in the source directory with the prefix `run_`, and
they are executed in alphabetical order.

- **`run_` scripts**: These scripts are executed every time you run [`chezmoi
  apply`][apply-command].
- **`run_onchange_` scripts**: These scripts are only executed if their content
has changed since the last time they were run successfully.
- **`run_once_` scripts**: These scripts are executed once for each unique
version of the content. If the script is a template, the content is hashed after
template execution. chezmoi tracks the content's SHA256 hash and stores it in a
database. If the content has been run successfully before (even under a
different filename), the script will not run again unless the content itself
changes.

Scripts break chezmoi's declarative approach and should be used sparingly.
All scripts should be idempotent, including `run_onchange_` and `run_once_` scripts.

Scripts are normally run while chezmoi updates your dotfiles. For example,
`run_b.sh` will be run after updating `a.txt` and before updating `c.txt`.
To run scripts before or after the updates, use the `before_` or `after_`
attributes, respectively, e.g., `run_once_before_install-password-manager.sh`.

Scripts must be created manually in the source directory, typically by running
[`chezmoi cd`][cd-command] and then creating a file with a `run_` prefix. There
is no need to set the executable bit on the script.

Scripts with the `.tmpl` suffix are treated as templates, with the usual
template variables available. If the template resolves to only whitespace
or an empty string, the script will not be executed, which is useful for
disabling scripts dynamically.

When executing a script, chezmoi generates the script contents in a file in a
temporary directory with the executable bit set and then executes it using `exec(3)`.
As a result, the script must either include a `#!` line or be an executable binary.
Script working directory is set to the first existing parent directory in the
destination tree.

If a `.chezmoiscripts` directory exists at the root of the source directory,
scripts in this directory are executed as normal scripts, without creating
a corresponding directory in the target state.

In verbose mode, the scripts' contents are printed before execution. In dry-run
mode, scripts are not executed.

## Set environment variables

You can set extra environment variables for your scripts, hooks, and commands in
the `scriptEnv` section of your config file. For example, to set the `MY_VAR`
environment variable to `my_value`, specify:

<!-- example-formats -->
```toml title="~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml"
[scriptEnv]
    MY_VAR = "my_value"
```
<!-- /example-formats -->

chezmoi sets a number of environment variables when running scripts, including
`CHEZMOI=1` and common template data like `CHEZMOI_OS` and `CHEZMOI_ARCH`.

## Don't show scripts that would run in `chezmoi diff`/`chezmoi status`

By default, [`chezmoi diff`][diff-command] will print the contents of scripts
that would be run by [`chezmoi apply`][apply-command]. To exclude scripts from
the output of `chezmoi diff`, set `diff.exclude` in your configuration file, for
example:

<!-- example-formats -->
```toml title="~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml"
[diff]
    exclude = ["scripts"]
```
<!-- /example-formats -->

Similarly, [`chezmoi status`][status-command] will print the names of the
scripts that it will execute with the status `R`. This can similarly disabled by
setting `status.exclude` to `["scripts"]` in your configuration file.

## Install packages with scripts

Change to the source directory and create a file called
`run_onchange_install-packages.sh`. In this file create your package
installation script, e.g.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
sudo apt install ripgrep
```

The next time you run [`chezmoi apply`][apply-command] or [`chezmoi
update`][update-command] this script will be run. As it has the `run_onchange_`
prefix, it will not be run again unless its contents change, for example if you
add more packages to be installed.

This script can also be a template. For example, if you create
`run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl` with the contents:

``` title="~/.local/share/chezmoi/run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl"
{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}
#!/bin/sh
sudo apt install ripgrep
{{ else if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
#!/bin/sh
brew install ripgrep
{{ end -}}
```

This will install `ripgrep` on both Debian/Ubuntu Linux systems and macOS.

## Run a script when the contents of another file changes

chezmoi's `run_` scripts are run every time you run [`chezmoi apply`][apply-command],
whereas `run_onchange_` scripts are run only when their contents have changed,
after executing them as templates. You can use this to cause a `run_onchange_`
script to run when the contents of another file has changed by including
a checksum of the other file's contents in the script.

For example, if your [dconf][dconf] settings are stored in `dconf.ini` in your
source directory then you can make [`chezmoi apply`][apply-command] only load
them when the contents of `dconf.ini` has changed by adding the following script
as `run_onchange_dconf-load.sh.tmpl`:

``` title="~/.local/share/chezmoi/run_onchange_dconf-load.sh.tmpl"
#!/bin/bash

# dconf.ini hash: {{ include "dconf.ini" | sha256sum }}
dconf load / < {{ joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "dconf.ini" | quote }}
```

As the SHA256 sum of `dconf.ini` is included in a comment in the script, the
contents of the script will change whenever the contents of `dconf.ini` are
changed, so chezmoi will re-run the script whenever the contents of `dconf.ini`
change.

In this example you should also add `dconf.ini` to [`.chezmoiignore`][ignore] so
chezmoi does not create `dconf.ini` in your home directory.

## Clear the state of all `run_onchange_` and `run_once_` scripts

chezmoi stores whether and when `run_onchange_` and `run_once_` scripts have
been run successfully in its persistent state.

To clear the state of `run_onchange_` scripts, run:

```sh
chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState
```

To clear the state of `run_once_` scripts, run:

```sh
chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
```

[apply-command]: /reference/commands/apply.md
[cd-command]: /reference/commands/cd.md
[diff-command]: /reference/commands/diff.md
[status-command]: /reference/commands/status.md
[update-command]: /reference/commands/update.md
[dconf]: https://wiki.gnome.org/Projects/dconf
[ignore]: /reference/special-files/chezmoiignore.md

```

What the documents now say:
- **Your decisions:**
  - the open-files limit is soft 32768 and hard 65536;
  - pipx is synced to the 28 installed venvs;
  - krew has a shared list plus a list per system;
  - Vundle is kept and YouCompleteMe is not built;
  - the report covers brew, pipx and krew;
  - scripts are numbered 0x/1x/2x/3x/9x, with the vim plugins at 21.
- **Corrections to the old design:**
  - paths now start with `home/`;
  - the base commit is `6bf6881`;
  - the rename claim at line 23 is fixed: a renamed script gets a new state key and runs once;
  - the `whosthere` example is fixed, because brew-file ignores casks on Linux;
  - the `10-brew` row and the darwin `brew bundle` placement are updated.
- **Spec:**
  - new undeclared pipx and krew scenarios;
  - new krew scenarios (Linux list, macOS list, moving a plugin between lists);
  - sudo's password prompt is allowed;
  - the Debian guard has its `--override-data` test;
  - a new "unrelated change leaves the script alone" scenario;
  - the live read-only harness mode is named.
- **Tasks:**
  - new groups for the `TODO.md`, data and pipx commits;
  - the 5.4 proof is `status --include=scripts` plus the dry run;
  - the harness allow-list is spelled out, with `brew file edit` and `brew file cat` excluded.

## Two places where I deviated from the plan you approved

1. **The decrypt script does not embed `{{ .chezmoi.executable }}`.** It would hold the versioned Cellar path of chezmoi, so every brew upgrade of chezmoi would change the rendered script and make it pending again. That is exactly the churn this change removes. It uses `chezmoi` from `PATH`, as today. Getting the binary onto `PATH` on a fresh machine stays with `fresh-machine-bootstrap`.
2. **The helper is included with `{{ template "script-lib.sh" (dict "name" "<script>" "root" .) }}`.** The design said `"script-lib.sh" .`. The helper needs the script name for its log prefix, and it needs `brew.prefix` for `load_brew`. Without `load_brew`, the mise, pipx and krew scripts would not find their tools right after a first Homebrew install.

## Facts I checked before writing them down

- chezmoi sets `CHEZMOI=1` for scripts, and a script that renders empty is not run.
- The config's `env` table does reach scripts, so the brew script exports no brew-file variables.
- `brew file clean --dry-run` printed only `$ brew cleanup` and `$ rm -rf <cache>` here, with or without the hook's `TOP_PACKAGES` value. Nothing is undeclared among the formulae and taps.
- That `brew file clean --dry-run` run was the only live command in this step, and it changed nothing.
- No private value was inferable from any command.

Commit 2 is committed (`ddddb3c`). Commit 3 is ready and not committed, so I need your go on its message.

```text
feat(chezmoi:scripts): add a shared script helper and package data
```

**What it contains (4 files):**
- **`home/.chezmoitemplates/script-lib.sh` (new):**
  - strict mode, `log`, `warn`, `have`;
  - `run`, which prints instead of executing under `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`;
  - `as_root <why> <command...>`;
  - `load_brew`;
  - `report_undeclared`;
  - a warning when the dry-run variable is set under chezmoi (`CHEZMOI=1`).
- **`home/.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`:**
  - new `packages.linux.apt` (12 packages);
  - new `system.limits.nofile` (32768 soft, 65536 hard);
  - new `vim.ycm_build: false`;
  - new `brew.prefix`;
  - the empty `dpkgs` key is gone.
- **`design.md`, `tasks.md`:** the helper's final shape, and ticks for 1.2, 2.1 to 2.4.

**Checked:**
- The helper renders and passes `bash -n` and `shellcheck -s bash` with no findings, using the mise copy of shellcheck 0.11.0.
- The six existing scripts still render against the new data.
- `chezmoi -S <worktree> data` shows the new keys.
- `openspec validate make-install-scripts-idempotent --strict` passes.

**Change from the approved plan:** the krew lists (`common`, `linux`, `darwin`) move from this commit to the krew script's commit (4.4). The old krew script reads the Linux list, so splitting it here would silently shrink what it installs until it is replaced.

**What the harness found.**
- **Setup:**
  - the harness is in `/tmp/opencode/scripts-test/` (mode 0700);
  - it has isolated and live read-only modes;
  - `brew file install` and `mise install` are rewritten to their dry-run forms;
  - `sudo` is never executed.
- **Live run:** machine state was identical before and after (360 formulae, 1 cask, 139 mise tools). Refused calls were logged, and the sudo stub failed as designed.
- **`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`:**
  - In a bare environment, `brew file install --dry-run` lists 20 installed tap formulae as missing.
  - Cause: Homebrew keeps its trust file under `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and looks in `~/.homebrew` when the variable is unset.
  - With the variable set, the dry run lists nothing.
  - `load_brew` now exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `~/.config`), and the design records why.
  - Without this, the first real run under ssh, cron or `env -i` would have tried to reinstall 20 formulae.

**One mistake to disclose.** My throwaway test of the helper called the real `sudo true`, because I ran it with a bare `PATH` instead of through the harness. It failed at once ("a password is required", stdin was `/dev/null`), so nothing was elevated or changed. The brief makes any real `sudo` a stop-and-ask, even for a check. A failed attempt may have left an authentication-failure line in the system log. From now on, every script test goes through `run.sh`, where `sudo` is always the stub. I'll include this in my report to the orchestrator.

If the message is fine, I'll commit and move to commit 4, the pipx sync.

def extract_venv_metadata(spec_metadata_file: Path) -> Iterator[PipxMetadata]:
    try:
        spec: Final = load_spec_file(spec_metadata_file)
    except json.decoder.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        msg = "The spec metadata file is an invalid JSON file."
        raise PipxError(msg) from exc

    venvs_metadata_dict: Final = spec.get("venvs")
    if not venvs_metadata_dict:
        msg = "No packages found in the spec metadata file."
        raise PipxError(msg)
    if not isinstance(venvs_metadata_dict, dict):
        msg = "The spec metadata file is invalid."
        raise PipxError(msg)

    for package_path_name, entry in venvs_metadata_dict.items():
        venv_dir = paths.ctx.venvs.joinpath(package_path_name)
        venv_metadata = PipxMetadata(venv_dir, read=False)
        venv_metadata.from_dict(entry["metadata"])
        yield venv_metadata


def generate_package_spec(package_info: PackageInfo) -> str:
    """Generate more precise package spec from package info."""
    if not package_info.package_or_url:
        msg = f"A package spec is not available for {package_info.package}"
        raise PipxError(msg)

    if package_info.package == package_info.package_or_url:
        return f"{package_info.package}=={package_info.package_version}"
    return package_info.package_or_url


def get_python_interpreter(
    source_interpreter: Path | None,
) -> str | None:
    """Get appropriate python interpreter."""
    if source_interpreter is not None and source_interpreter.is_file():
        return str(source_interpreter)

    source_interpreter: Path | None,
) -> str | None:

the file reaches PAM login sessions (TTY, ssh), not the systemd user manager.\n# limits hash: {{ .system.limits | toJson | sha256sum }}\n{{ template \"script-lib.sh\" (dict \"name\" \"system-limits\" \"root\" .) }}\n\nfile=/etc/security/limits.d/ulimit.conf\nsoft={{ $soft }}\nhard={{ $hard }}\nwant=$(printf '* soft nofile %s\\n* hard nofile %s\\n' \"$soft\" \"$hard\")\n\nif [ -f \"$file\" ] && [ \"$(cat \"$file\")\" = \"$want\" ]; then\n  warn \"$file holds soft ${current_soft:-none} and hard ${current_hard:-none}, above the declared $soft and $hard: left unchanged\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nas_root \"write $file (soft $soft, hard $hard)\" install -m 0644 /dev/stdin \"$file\" <<< \"$want\"\n{{ end -}}\n"

**Output:**
```
### Shared helper

`.chezmoitemplates/script-lib.sh` is included right after the shebang with `{{ template "script-lib.sh" (dict "name" "<script>" "root" .) }}`; it has no shebang of its own.
It provides:

- `set -euo pipefail`;
- `log` and `warn` (prefixed with the script name, to stderr);
- `have` (`command -v` wrapper);
- `run` (executes, or prints the command with `printf %q` when `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`; read-only queries are written without `run`, so they still execute);
- `as_root <why> <command...>` (logs why, then calls `run sudo`, or `run` directly when already root);
- `load_brew` (gives the script the environment of the user's shell: it exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` with the default `~/.config` and evaluates `brew shellenv` from `brew.prefix` when `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` is not set, so that scripts after a first Homebrew install find the tools);
- `report_undeclared <what> <installed> <declared>` (lists installed names that are not declared, removes nothing);
- a warning when the dry-run variable is set while `CHEZMOI=1`.

`load_brew` exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` because Homebrew keeps its trust file in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/homebrew` and looks in `~/.homebrew` when the variable is unset.
Without the file, third-party taps are untrusted and brew-file lists the 20 installed tap formulae of the Brewfile as missing (found with the live harness: `brew file install --dry-run` printed a `brew install` line for them in a bare environment, and printed nothing once `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was set).
A shell that sourced `rc.d` has the variable, but ssh commands, cron and `env -i` do not.

An edit to the helper changes every script that includes it, so each runs once more; all of them are no-ops on a provisioned machine.

```

```text
fix(chezmoi:scripts): make before scripts idempotent and guarded

The shared helper no longer embeds the Homebrew prefix, so a data change
re-runs only the scripts that read that data.
```

**What it contains (8 files):**
- **`run_onchange_before_00-prerequisites.sh.tmpl`** (renamed from `00-pre-requesites`):
  - It renders empty unless the os-release `id` is `debian` or `id_like` names it, and when the apt list is empty.
  - It checks each package with `dpkg-query`, and calls sudo (`apt-get update` plus one install) only for missing ones.
  - Its trigger is a hash of `packages.linux.apt`.
- **`run_onchange_before_01-decrypt-private-key.sh.tmpl`** (renamed):
  - It uses `$HOME`, has no literal path, and still asks for the passphrase only when the identity is missing.
  - It runs chezmoi through `CHEZMOI_EXECUTABLE`, which chezmoi sets for its scripts. I confirmed that in chezmoi's source. The design had said "`chezmoi` from `PATH`", and this is better.
  - It writes the identity with umask 077. Under your 027 umask the file was briefly group-readable before the `chmod`. This is new behaviour.
- **`run_onchange_before_02-system-limits.sh.tmpl`** (new):
  - It reads `system.limits.nofile` (32768 soft, 65536 hard).
  - It checks at render time that the values are whole numbers with `0 < soft <= hard`.
  - It exits when the file matches. It warns and leaves the file alone when the file holds a higher or non-numeric limit. Otherwise it writes with `sudo install -m 0644 /dev/stdin`.
- **`script-lib.sh`:** now `template "script-lib.sh" "<name>"` and `load_brew <prefix>`. See the next section.
- **`design.md` and `tasks.md`:** a "Before scripts" section, and tasks 3.1 to 3.3 ticked.

**A fix to my own helper, folded into this commit.**
- My trigger check showed the helper embedded `brew.prefix` in its text, so changing the prefix would have re-run the apt, limits and decrypt scripts. The spec says an unrelated change must leave a script alone.
- Now the helper holds only the script name, and the scripts that use brew will pass the prefix themselves.
- Matrix after the fix: an apt change re-runs only the prerequisites, a limits change only the limits script, and krew, `vim.ycm_build` and `brew.prefix` changes re-run none of the three.

**Proof (all through the harness, `sudo` always the stub):**
- **Live mode, on this laptop:**
  - prerequisites exits 0 with 12 of 12 installed and no sudo call;
  - limits finds the file already matching;
  - decrypt finds the identity present;
  - the sudo and refused logs are empty for all three.
- **Prerequisites, isolated:**
  - with `git` and `snapper` missing, the sudo log shows exactly `apt-get update` and one `apt-get install -qy git snapper`;
  - the dry run prints the same two commands and calls nothing.
- **Debian guard:**
  - kali, debian, ubuntu and linuxmint render the script;
  - fedora, rocky, arch, alpine and macOS render empty;
  - an empty apt list renders empty.
- **Limits, isolated** (the path aimed at a scratch file):
  - matching file: no sudo;
  - file absent or holding lower values: one `install` call, and the content afterwards is the declared pair;
  - declared soft 16384 under a file holding 32768: a warning and the file unchanged;
  - file holding `unlimited`: a warning and the file unchanged;
  - dry run: the command is printed and the file is unchanged;
  - soft above hard, soft 0 or a non-number: the render fails, and with no `system` data the render is empty.
- **Decrypt, isolated:**
  - the identity absent gives one decrypt call, via `PATH` or via `CHEZMOI_EXECUTABLE`;
  - the umask seen by the call is 0077, and the file ends at mode 600;
  - the dry run creates nothing.
  - The real passphrase prompt was not exercised, because fixtures stand in for chezmoi.
- **Static checks:**
  - all three pass `bash -n` and `shellcheck -s bash`;
  - the sources have no literal home or source path and no escaped actions;

#!/bin/bash
brew_installed=1
if ! which brew > /dev/null 2>&1;then
  brew_installed=0
  echo Homebrew is not installed!
  echo Install now...
  echo /bin/bash -c \"\$\(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh\)\"
  /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
  ret=$?
  if [ $ret -ne 0 ];then
    echo Failed to install Homebrew... please check your environment
    exit $ret
  fi
  echo

  if echo "$OSTYPE" | grep -q darwin;then
    arc=$(uname -m)
    if [ "$arc" = "x86_64" ];then
      paths=(/usr/local /opt/homebrew)
    else
      paths=(/opt/homebrew /usr/local)
    fi
  else
    paths=(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew "$HOME/.linuxbrew" /opt/homebrew /usr/local)
  fi

  for path in "${paths[@]}";do
    if [ -f "$path/bin/brew" ];then
      export PATH="$path/sbin:$path/bin:$PATH"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

echo
echo Install Brew-file...

brew install rcmdnk/file/brew-file

if [ $brew_installed -eq 0 ];then
  # Do not check stray files.
  # linux_sandbox is excluded, too: Homebrew 6 requires rootless Bubblewrap
  # and unprivileged user namespaces for the Linux sandbox, which are not
  # always available (e.g. GitHub Actions runners), while brew still works
  # without the sandbox.
  read -ra checks < <(brew doctor --list-checks | grep -vE '(dylibs|static_libs|headers|cask|brew_git_branch|linux_sandbox)'|tr '\n' ' ')
  if ! brew doctor "${checks[@]}";then
    echo Check brew environment!
    exit 1
  fi
fi

## `home/.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10-brew.sh.tmpl`, Linux branch

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Brewfile hash: {{ include "dot_config/brewfile/Brewfile" | sha256sum }}
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "brew" }}

load_brew '<brew.prefix>'
brewfile=${HOMEBREW_BREWFILE:-$HOME/.config/brewfile/Brewfile}
[ -f "$brewfile" ] || { warn "$brewfile is missing"; exit 1; }

if ! have brew || ! brew file version > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  # cache sudo credentials (the one place a password prompt can appear), then Homebrew's installer
  [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] && as_root "cache sudo credentials for the Homebrew installer" -v
  run env NONINTERACTIVE=1 bash -c 'curl -fsSL <brew-file install.sh> | bash'
  load_brew '<brew.prefix>'
fi
have brew || { dry_run && exit 0; warn "brew is still missing after the installer"; exit 1; }

run brew file install
# drift report, read only: formulae and taps from `brew file clean --dry-run`, casks by comparison
report_undeclared "brew formulae" ... ; report_undeclared "brew taps" ... ; report_undeclared "brew casks" ...
# rustup default stable only when `rustup default` reports no default; gh login is only a warning
```

I abbreviated the report and rustup parts above. The darwin branch is the old `brew bundle` call with a guard for a missing `brew`.

## Proof (all through the harness; `sudo` is always the stub)

- **Live, on this laptop:**
  - exit 0, and the sudo and refused logs are empty;
  - `brew file install` is rewritten to its dry run and finds nothing to install;
  - `whosthere` is reported as an undeclared cask;
  - formulae, casks, taps, mise, rustup, pipx and krew counts are identical before and after;
  - no file under `~/.config/brewfile`, `~/.config/homebrew`, `~/.rustup` or `~/.cargo` is newer than the start marker.
- **Isolated:**
  - **Nothing missing:** no mutating call.
  - **Drift fixture:** names two formulae, one tap and one cask, and makes zero uninstall or untap calls.
  - **Dry run:** prints `would run: brew file install` and does not call it.
  - **No default Rust toolchain:** `rustup default stable` is called.
  - **gh logged out:** a warning, not a failure.
  - **Brewfile not deployed:** exit 1 before any brew call.
  - **Homebrew missing:** `sudo -v` goes through the sudo stub, the installer is printed, and the script fails loudly. The dry run exits 0.
  - **Fresh machine, against a throwaway prefix:** the "installer" creates a fake brew, `load_brew` finds it, and the script carries on.
  - **`load_brew` with `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` unset:** it evaluates `shellenv` and exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.
  - **darwin:** `brew bundle --file=/dev/stdin` receives `brew "git"` and `cask "google-chrome"`.
- **Static:** `bash -n` and `shellcheck -s bash` are clean on the Linux and darwin renders. An unlisted OS renders empty, and `openspec validate --strict` passes.

## Three things the tests found

1. **A harness hazard, fixed before it could bite.** `brew shellenv` always prepends the real Homebrew directory to `PATH`. A script that calls `load_brew` under my harness would have put the real `brew` ahead of the stubs. The harness now always passes `HOMEBREW_PREFIX`, so `load_brew` never evaluates `shellenv` there, and `-P` (prefix unset) refuses a script that embeds the real prefix. No real brew command ran in any test.
2. **A harness allow-list gap.** `brew file version` calls `brew -v` internally. My stub refused it, the script took the "brew-file missing" branch and tried to cache sudo credentials, and the `sudo` stub failed it. The machine did not change. I added `brew -v`, a read-only version print, to the allow-list.
3. **A design change from the plan.** The plan said the Homebrew installer would run with `NONINTERACTIVE=1` and that its sudo would stay outside `as_root`. But with `NONINTERACTIVE=1` Homebrew needs cached sudo credentials. The script now caches them first with `sudo -v` through `as_root`. That is the one password prompt, and it shows in the sudo log. Without a terminal or passwordless sudo it fails before installing anything. It's in the design.

## Questions

1. **Is the brew script fine as it is?** If so I'll continue with `11-mise`, `12-pipx`, `13-krew` (with the krew data) and `21-vim-plugins`, remove `05-install` and `10-install-packages`, and propose commit 6 as one commit with the message from the plan.
2. **Missing `brew file` command.** The script also treats a failing `brew file version` as "brew-file missing" and runs the installer. That covers a machine that has Homebrew but no brew-file, at the cost of one extra call. Keep it?

- **Removed:** `run_onchange_before_05-install.sh.tmpl` and `run_onchange_before_10-install-packages.sh.tmpl`.

## Decisions and findings to confirm

1. **Vim needs `-N`.**
   - In vim's silent Ex mode, my first version printed E10 errors from Vundle's own autoload file and exited 1. Ex mode starts vi-compatible, so line continuations stop working.
   - On a healthy machine that would have printed the "plugins may be incomplete" warning on every run, and the real `PluginInstall` might have misbehaved too.
   - The command is now `vim -N -Es -n -u ~/.vimrc -i NONE +PluginInstall +qall`. With `-N` the exit is 0, and `exists(":PluginInstall")` is 2 against your real vimrc. Vim wrote no file during that check.
   - The vimrc has no `set nocompatible` of its own.
2. **A missing manager is a skip.** mise, pipx, krew and vim print a warning and exit 0, like the VSCodium script. The drawback is that chezmoi then counts the script as run until its input changes. Missing deployed inputs (Brewfile, `packages.json`, vimrc, the Vundle external) exit 1, so chezmoi retries. Do you want this split?
3. **`brew.prefix` changes re-run five scripts.** They pass it to `load_brew`, so they do read it. That matches the spec: a script re-runs when an input it acts on changes.

## Proof

- **Full harness run, 41 cases: 41 pass.** 33 are isolated and 8 are live on this laptop, covering every script except the not-yet-rewritten VSCodium and bat scripts. `/tmp/opencode/scripts-test/all.sh` repeats the whole run with one command.
- **Live mode:**
  - all 8 scripts exit 0, with no sudo call and no refused call;
  - counts are identical before and after: 360 formulae, 1 cask, 28 taps, 139 mise tools, 28 pipx venvs, 7 krew plugins and 71 extensions;
  - the limits file is unchanged.
- **Isolated mode:**
  - **Installs:** a missing pipx venv, krew plugin or apt package triggers exactly one install call. The pipx spec handed over holds only the missing venvs, with full metadata.
  - **Dry run:** prints the commands and calls nothing.
  - **Skips:** a missing tool is skipped as described above.
  - **YouCompleteMe:** it builds only when `vim.ycm_build` is true and the library is missing.
  - **Undeclared reports:** the undeclared formulae, tap and cask are named, and nothing is removed.
- **Krew render:**
  - Linux gives all 7 plugins.
  - macOS gives the 4 shared ones, plus any plugin added to the darwin list, without duplicates.
  - Windows, an empty list and a null list render empty.
  - Moving a plugin between lists leaves the rendered script identical.
- **Triggers:** editing the Brewfile, mise config, `packages.json` or vimrc re-runs only the matching script. Unrelated edits (tmux config, bat config for now) re-run none. A change to a data key re-runs only the scripts that read it. The one extra hit, the decrypt script, comes from the scratch copy's different source path.
- **Static:** `bash -n` and `shellcheck -s bash` are clean on all 10 rendered scripts, and `openspec validate --strict` passes. The scripts have no literal home path and no dashes. The only escaped action left is in the bat script, which is commit 8's job.
- **`chezmoi -S <worktree> status --include=scripts`:** 9 scripts pending, namely 00, 01, 02, 10, 11, 12, 13, 20 and 21.

## Problems in my own harness, found and fixed during this commit

- **Leak in isolated mode:**
  - `-a vim` (vim absent) only removed the stub, so the real `/usr/bin/vim` ran once in an isolated test, with the fixture vimrc, `-n` and `-i NONE`. It ended with E492, and nothing changed.
  - Isolated mode now uses a `PATH` of the stubs plus a directory of basic utilities, so no real copy of a stubbed tool can be reached.
- **Python:**
  - `brew-file` is a Python script, so adding a `python3` stub made the live brew run refuse it. I allowed `python3` only for brew-file's three read-only forms.
  - The first forwarding attempt looped through a mise shim. It now goes to `/usr/bin/python3`, the one the shim falls back to.
- **No real command changed anything.**

## Not exercised, to be clear about the limits

- The real `pipx install-all`, `kubectl krew install`, `mise install`, Vundle `PluginInstall` and the Homebrew installer never ran. The harness proves each call, its arguments and its guard. The live `mise install` was only its `--dry-run-code` form, and the vim step in live mode only checked that your vimrc loads and Vundle defines the command.
- `pipx list` is not write-free: it writes a log file under `~/.local/state/pipx` and touches lock files in the venvs directory, all inside `$HOME`. No venv content changed.

## Assistant (Build · Claude Sonnet 5.5 · 15.6s)

The new `packages.json` is deployed, and I have the facts for both decisions. Commit 6 is still uncommitted. It waits on your two choices below, and then on your go for its message.

## Deployed

- `~/.config/pipx/packages.json` was applied as a single target with `--exclude=scripts,externals`.
- It is now mode 640 (it was 664, so this follows your umask 027), 28 venvs, and in sync with the source.
- The pipx script run live on this laptop now says "all declared venvs are installed" and lists no undeclared venv.
- The full harness still passes: 41 of 41.

## Correction to what I told you

Last turn I wrote that the vimrc has no `set nocompatible` of its own. That was wrong. It has one at line 665. Vundle is loaded at line 21, so the order is the problem.

## Decision 1: vim and `-N`

**What goes wrong.**
- Vim's silent Ex mode (`-Es`, which a script needs) starts with the `compatible` option on.
- In that state vim does not join the `\` continuation lines in Vundle's own files.
- The vimrc loads Vundle at line 21 and turns `compatible` off only at line 665. That is too late.
- In an interactive vim you never see this, because vim resets `compatible` before it reads a vimrc.

**What I measured with your real vimrc** (`:command` listing after startup):

| Command | without `-N` | with `-N` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:Plugin` | defined with an empty body | `call vundle#config#bundle(<args>)` |
| `:PluginInstall` | defined with an empty body | `call vundle#installer#new(...)` |
| vim exit code | 1 | 0 |

Without `-N`, none of the `Plugin 'x'` lines declare anything and `+PluginInstall` does nothing. The script would only print a warning.

**Your options:**
1. **Keep `-N` in the script (my recommendation).** One flag, documented in the design, and no edit to your vimrc.
2. **Move `set nocompatible` to the top of the vimrc,** as Vundle's documentation asks. Then `-N` isn't needed. It edits your vimrc, which this change doesn't otherwise touch. The design now says this belongs to `cleanup-dead-config`.
3. **Drop the vim plugin script.** You already chose to keep it.

## Decision 2: "missing manager is a skip"

**What chezmoi does** (from its documentation):
- A `run_onchange_` script is recorded as run when it exits 0.
- If it exits non-zero, it is not recorded, it runs again at the next apply, and the apply stops at that script unless `--keep-going` is passed.

**Right now,** mise, pipx, krew and vim print a warning and exit 0 when their tool is missing. Their input hash is then recorded. When the tool shows up later, nothing re-runs the script until its input changes (a Brewfile edit, a vimrc edit, and so on). The warning appears once, in the apply output, and `chezmoi status` shows nothing pending afterwards.

**When a tool can be missing,** from what I checked:
- **`brew-file` partial failure.** `brew file install` only logs a warning for a formula that fails to install and carries on, so the script after it can find a tool missing. This is the realistic case on a fresh machine.
- **`jq`.**
  - The pipx script needs it.
  - On this machine it is `/usr/bin/jq`, installed by apt as a dependency of `clevis-luks` and `fwupd`.
  - Nothing in this repository declares it: it is neither in the Brewfile nor in the apt list.
  - Kali has it by chance, but a plain Debian may not.
  - With skip semantics, a fresh machine without `jq` would silently never get its pipx venvs.
- **`vim`.** It is a brew dependency of `ttyd`, not declared itself. It disappears if `ttyd` leaves the Brewfile.
- **`kubectl`.** It comes from the `kubernetes-cli` formula or a mise shim. On this machine both work.
- **A machine that doesn't want a tool.** For example, a server without vim.

**Your options:**
- **A. Skip with exit 0 (what the scripts do now).**
  - The apply always completes.
  - A missing tool is forgotten until its input changes.
- **B. Fail with exit 1.**
  - Nothing is forgotten, and the script re-runs at every apply.
  - The apply stops at the first missing tool, and every apply fails on a machine that doesn't want that tool. Opting out would need a data flag.
- **C. Mixed (my recommendation).**
  - Fail (exit 1) for mise, pipx and krew, because the Brewfile declares them. Missing means a brew step went wrong, and you want to hear about it.
  - Skip for vim and codium, which this repository doesn't declare (VSCodium already skips today).
  - Declare `jq` in `packages.linux.apt`, since the pipx script needs it. That adds one declared package, which the brief lists as a non-goal, so it needs your go. The alternative is to drop `jq` from the pipx script and use `python3`.
- **D. Skip, but re-run when the tool appears.** Put `{{ not (empty (lookPath "mise")) }}` in the script's hash line. It's self-healing, but the hash then depends on the `PATH` of whoever runs the apply, so an interactive shell and cron could flip it. I don't recommend it.

## What I need from you

1. **Vim:** option 1, 2 or 3?
2. **Missing managers:** A, B, C or D? If C, do you want `jq` added to the apt list, or removed from the pipx script?

Once you answer I'll adjust the scripts, re-run the whole harness, and bring you commit 6's message again with those changes in it.

54: ## Decisions
55: 
56: ### New script set
57: 
58: Numbering by kind: 0x before, 1x package managers, 2x editors, 3x user setup (`manage-xdg-basics` takes 30, `add-mise-app-desktop-entries` takes 31), 9x caches.
59: 
60: | Script | Phase | Trigger (hashed input) | Does |
61: | --- | --- | --- | --- |

66: | `run_onchange_after_11-mise.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/mise/config.toml` | `mise install --yes` |
67: | `run_onchange_after_12-pipx.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/pipx/packages.json` | installs only venvs missing from `pipx list --short`, through a filtered copy of the spec file; reports undeclared venvs |
68: | `run_onchange_after_13-krew.sh.tmpl` | after | the combined plugin list | Linux and macOS; installs only missing plugins; reports undeclared plugins; renders empty when the list is empty |

73: Hash lines use `{{ include "<path>" | sha256sum }}` (paths relative to `home/`) or `{{ .<data> | toJson | sha256sum }}`; nothing escaped.
74: Package managers move to after-scripts so they read deployed files (Brewfile, `packages.json`, `vimrc`) instead of source paths, and so vim plugins install after Vundle (an external) and the vimrc exist.
75: The bat hash covers the external declarations, not the upstream theme files, which the weekly refresh may change without re-running the script.
